claims.text: Adding a low concentration of yttrium to high-entropy-alloy bond coats will enhance thermal-barrier-coating durability and reliability.
Yttrium doping will promote formation of an adherent, refined alumina scale.
The yttrium-promoted alumina scale will resist spallation during high-temperature cyclic oxidation.
High-entropy-alloy bond coats without yttrium exhibit standard oxidation resistance and typical spallation behavior under thermal cycling.
Cyclic oxidation at approximately 1100–1200°C in air is representative of turbine-engine operating conditions.
Thermal cycling and oxidation are the predominant degradation mechanisms under the stated conditions.
Yttrium segregates at the metal/oxide interface.
Interfacial yttrium segregation promotes a dense and uniform alumina scale.
Interfacial yttrium segregation increases alumina-scale adherence.
Yttrium acts as a reactive element that modifies alumina growth kinetics.
Yttrium refines grain boundaries in the alumina scale.
Yttrium reduces defect formation within the alumina scale.
The proposed changes to the alumina scale delay spallation and slow overall oxidation.
Yttrium-doped coatings will have less oxide spallation than undoped coatings.
Yttrium-doped coatings will exhibit slower thermally grown oxide growth than undoped coatings.
Yttrium doping will improve cyclic high-temperature durability by an estimated 20–30% relative to undoped coatings.
The beneficial effect will persist under cyclic oxidation up to approximately 1200°C when yttrium is within an optimal concentration range.
The beneficial effect may diminish above the optimal yttrium concentration or outside the tested temperature and environmental range.
Prior evidence supports improved durability from reactive-element doping.
